issues.description: Default base image constant is duplicated across three locations with no single source of truth
issues.detail: DEFAULT_BASE_IMAGE = 'python:3.12' is declared in backend/kale/pipeline.py, hardcoded as a fallback string 'python:3.12' in labextension/src/lib/Commands.ts (getDefaultBaseImage catch branch), and re-declared as DEFAULT_BASE_IMAGE = 'python:3.12' in labextension/src/widgets/cell-metadata/CellMetadataEditor.tsx. The whole point of introducing the constant is to centralize the value; having three independent copies means a future bump to python:3.13 will silently leave two stale literals behind. A literate reader cannot tell which is authoritative. Choose one source (the RPC) and let the others reference it; if a static fallback is truly needed, name and comment it as 'last-resort fallback only'.

issues.description: Semantic change to _set_base_image: empty-string fallback replaced by an opinionated default, with no test or migration note
issues.detail: Previously self.base_image = '' meant 'let kfp pick its default', which downstream KFP interpreted in its own way. Now it is hard-bound to 'python:3.12'. This is a behavior change for users who relied on kfp's default, and the invariant 'base_image is either user-specified or empty (= delegate to kfp)' is being replaced silently with 'base_image is always a concrete image string'. The template still has a chain (step.config.base_image or base_image or default_base_image), so the empty-string path was load-bearing for the 'no opinion' case. Either keep the empty sentinel and resolve the default at template time only, or state the new invariant explicitly in a comment and add a regression test.

issues.description: createBaseImageText now always renders, making '(default)' annotation appear even when no step name / not a step cell context — invariant for when this paragraph is shown was lost
issues.detail: Previously the function returned '' (no element) when this.props.baseImage was falsy; now it always returns a paragraph showing effectiveImage with '(default)'. The caller's expectation that this returned an empty node in the no-baseImage case is no longer true. This will produce visible 'Base Image: python:3.12 (default)' lines on cells where the previous UI was deliberately quiet. State the invariant 'we show base image text when the cell is a step' and gate the render on that, rather than always rendering with a default string.

issues.description: Replacing an inline Input with a Button + Dialog increases interaction cost from 1 click to 2-3 without measured justification
issues.detail: The old UI exposed Base Image as an inline text input (width 25%). The new UI hides editing behind a button labeled 'IMAGE' that opens a modal. This is a workflow regression for the common case (set a custom image quickly) traded for a benefit in the uncommon case (see what the default is). No measurement is presented that users were confused by the inline input. If the goal is 'show the default', a placeholder or helper text on the existing Input would have achieved the same with zero added clicks. Reconsider whether the dialog earns its complexity.

issues.description: Button labeled 'IMAGE' with title='Base Image' and width style of '5%' is unreadable and inconsistent with the literate-programming principle
issues.detail: The button has style={{ width: '5%' }} on a contained MUI Button containing the text 'IMAGE' — 5% width will almost certainly clip or overflow depending on container, and 'IMAGE' is shouty and ambiguous (image of what?). A serious reader of this code cannot tell what was intended. Use a meaningful label like 'Base Image' and let MUI size it, or use an icon button with an aria-label. Also the wrapping <div style={{ padding: 0, marginRight: '4px' }}> is a code smell — why a div with padding:0?

issues.description: RPC defined that returns a constant — round-trip to the backend for a value the frontend already hardcodes as fallback
issues.detail: get_default_base_image is a new RPC method whose only behavior is to import DEFAULT_BASE_IMAGE and return it. The frontend Commands.getDefaultBaseImage falls back to 'python:3.12' on error, so the network/kernel round-trip exists purely so the two literals stay in sync — but they don't (see duplication issue). If the intent is 'backend is the source of truth', remove the frontend fallback literal and surface an error state. If the intent is 'frontend can stand alone', drop the RPC. As written, the RPC pays cost without buying consistency.

issues.description: Local import inside get_default_base_image function obscures dependency and is not justified
issues.detail: The line `from kale.pipeline import DEFAULT_BASE_IMAGE` is placed inside the function body. There is no comment explaining why (circular import? lazy load?). pipeline is already imported at module scope in many sibling RPCs in this file presumably. A reader has to guess. Either hoist the import to module scope or add a one-line comment stating the reason for the local import.

issues.description: Reordering createLimitsText / createBaseImageText in render output changes visual order without explanation
issues.detail: The render block now emits createLimitsText() before createBaseImageText() where previously base image came first. This is a visible UI reordering with no comment justifying it. If the swap is intentional (e.g., to keep base image adjacent to a new element), state why; if it is accidental cleanup, revert. Small UI changes without rationale make future bisects harder.

issues.description: No tests added for the new behavior (default propagation through compiler template, RPC, or UI)
issues.detail: The PR introduces a new constant, a new compiler template variable, a new RPC, and new UI state — and no tests are visible in the diff exercising any of it. At minimum a unit test that the compiler renders default_base_image into the template when step.config.base_image and pipeline base_image are both unset would catch the silent regression of changing 'python:3.12' literal to a variable name. 'I have only proved it correct, not tried it' applies here in its negative form: nothing has been proved and nothing has been tried.

review.summary: The change introduces a sensible centralization (one DEFAULT_BASE_IMAGE constant) but then fails to centralize: the same literal 'python:3.12' is duplicated in pipeline.py, Commands.ts fallback, and CellMetadataEditor.tsx, defeating the purpose. The backend semantic change from '' to DEFAULT_BASE_IMAGE in _set_base_image is a real behavior change masquerading as a refactor and deserves a stated invariant and a test. The UI work trades an inline Input for a Button-plus-Dialog without measurement that the inline form was the problem, and createBaseImageText now always renders, breaking its prior 'empty when no image' contract. Decision label: UNDER-AUDITED with NEEDS-LITERATE-COMMENT — the algorithm of 'resolve default base image' is now spread across four layers (pipeline.py, RPC, frontend Commands, two UI components) with no single document of which layer owns the value and why. Tighten to one source of truth, gate the always-rendered paragraph, justify the dialog, and add at least one compiler-template test.
